title: Designing a smart home
blurb: Planning wiring, sensors, and automation before the walls go up.
suggestions: What should I plan before construction?
Should I add a voice assistant?

slides.title: Plan before the slab
bullets: Conduits are cheap now, expensive later
Run extra pipes to every room
slides.notes: The cheapest time to plan automation is before construction. Empty conduits cost very little during the slab and walls stage, and running a spare pipe to every room saves breaking walls later.
slides.narration: The best time to plan a smart home is before the slab is poured. Conduits are cheap now and very expensive later.

slides.title: Lighting without false ceilings
bullets: Group circuits by scene, not by room
slides.notes: Without a false ceiling, lighting comes from surface profiles and wall washers. Grouping circuits by scene rather than room, and choosing dimmable drivers upfront, makes automation simple later.
slides.narration: Without a false ceiling, you lean on surface profiles and wall washers, and group circuits by scene rather than by room.

slides.title: Sensors that earn their place
slides.notes: Not every sensor is worth it. Motion sensors in corridors and bathrooms, contacts on main doors, and leak sensors under sinks give the most value for the least effort.
slides.narration: Only a few sensors really earn their place: motion in corridors and bathrooms, contacts on the main doors, and leak sensors under sinks.

slides.title: The control layer
bullets: A local hub keeps working offline
slides.notes: A local hub keeps everything running when the internet drops. The phone app handles everyday control, but physical switches should always work too, so guests are never stuck.
slides.narration: A local hub keeps things working offline. The phone app handles daily control, but the physical switches must always work.

slides.title: Voice, later
bullets: Add voice once routines are stable
Keep wake words off in bedrooms
slides.notes: Voice is best added last, once routines are stable and you know what you actually ask for. Starting with the app and sensors avoids building voice commands nobody uses.
slides.narration: Voice comes last. Get the app and sensors right first, then add voice once you know which routines you actually use.

slides.title: A phased budget
slides.notes: Splitting the budget into phases keeps it manageable: conduits and boxes during construction, lighting and switches at finishing, and sensors and automation once you've lived in the house.
slides.narration: Finally, budget in three phases: conduits during construction, lighting at finishing, and automation once you've moved in.
